label: early original-phase steps after s/1 in sequences starting with t/k/p (weak)
explanation: Sparse feature (0.03% of steps). 91% of activation mass is in the original phase at t=3..6, never at t<3; there is a small tail at the delimiter and first copy step. Activation is enriched when the sequence starts with t (11x), k or p, when s or 1 was input one or two steps earlier (10-14x), and when the current input is d/h/y/o/s/0. None of these, alone or combined, gives usable precision: the best conjunction (first token t, s/1 in the previous two inputs, t=3..5) reaches only F1 0.15 on dev (P 0.11, R 0.28), and broader versions get ~0.8 recall at under 1% precision. The feature looks like a sparse combinatorial readout of the early-sequence hidden state rather than any single token or position property. It does not fire at t=0..2 or in later copy steps (recall_idx >= 2).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=t (+5.86), orig0=k (+5.21), prev_tok=1 (+4.65), orig1=t (+3.82), prev_tok=s (+3.80), prev2_tok=1 (+3.64). Lower it: correct=1 (-6.07), prev3_tok=- (-4.36), phase=2 (-3.60), prev3_tok=k (-3.20).
